citations.quote: The review team recommends accelerated approval of glofitamab-gxbm, a bispecific CD20-directed T-cell engager, for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (DLBCL, NOS) or large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL) arising from follicular lymphoma, after two or more lines of systemic therapy.

Glofitamab-gxmb, also referred to as glofitamab, binds to both CD20 expressed on B cells and to the CD3 receptor expressed on T cells, causing T-cell activation and proliferation, secretion of cytokines, and the lysis of CD20-expressing B cells.

citations.quote: Adverse reactions (ARs) occurred in 99% of patients, including Grade 3 or higher ARs in 64% of patients. ARs resulted in interruption of glofitamab in 19% of patients and discontinuation in 7%. Serious ARs occurred in 48% of patients, including from CRS, infection, and tumor flare, and fatal ARs occurred in 5%. The most common non-laboratory ARs (\ge 20\%) were CRS (70%, including Grade 2 CRS in 14%, Grade 3 in 2.8%, and Grade 4 in 1.4%), musculoskeletal pain (21%), fatigue (20%), and rash (20%); grade 3 or 4 laboratory abnormalities occurring in \ge 20\% of patients included lymphocyte count decreased, phosphate decreased, neutrophils decreased, fibrinogen decreased, and uric acid increased. Immune effector cell associated neurotoxicity (ICANS) was reported 4.8% of patients.

detail.text: Boxed warning for Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS), including serious or fatal reactions; premedicate and use step-up dosing to reduce risk

citations.quote: ## WARNING: CYTOKINE RELEASE SYNDROME

Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS), including serious or fatal reactions, can occur in patients receiving COLUMVI. Premedicate before each dose, and initiate treatment with the COLUMVI step-up dosing schedule to reduce the risk of CRS. Withhold COLUMVI until CRS resolves or permanently discontinue based on severity. (2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4, 5.1)

citations.quote: 4464-1 Complete a randomized clinical trial that evaluates the clinical benefit of glofitamab in patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The trial should compare glofitamab in combination with gemcitabine and oxaliplatin (GemOx) to rituximab in combination with GemOx for patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The primary endpoint should be overall survival with secondary endpoints that include progression-free survival and response rate.

requirement.text: 4464-2: Conduct a study assessing efficacy and safety of glofitamab in pediatric patients 6 months or older with relapsed or refractory non-Hodgkin lymphoma (deferred pediatric study under PREA)

citations.quote: 4464-2 Conduct a study assessing the efficacy and safety of glofitamab in pediatric patients 6 months or older with relapsed or refractory non-Hodgkin lymphoma. The safety endpoints should evaluate safety and tolerability of glofitamab monotherapy and in combination with standard chemotherapy and identify the recommended dosage. The efficacy endpoints should evaluate activity as assessed by response rate and durability of response.
